body.statement:
The asserted whole-array uniform selector-conditional convergence is false under \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), and its failure can be maximal even inside the stationary independent-over-time square subclass satisfying Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5, supplementary conditions D.1--D.10, and the fixed-role full-rank condition for both predeclared roles.  Specifically, fix
\[
 0<\kappa<\frac{6373}{15369},\qquad
 0<\nu<\frac{39}{625},
\]
and a sufficiently large finite moment envelope.  For every sufficiently large integer \(q\), there is a whole triangular array \((P_j^{(q)})_{j\geq1}\in\mathcal M(0)\) with constant treatment effect \(\Delta_t=\tau\), conditionally independent factor-measurement errors, and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{39}{625},\qquad
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1\quad(s\in\mathcal S),
\]
whose stacked limiting covariance is singular, but for
\[
 T_q=
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
      {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
\]
one has
\[
 \lim_{q\to\infty}
 \mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}\!\left[
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
  \left|
   \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}\{T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right]=1.
\]
Thus positive limiting marginal variances, coordinatewise studentization, a logarithm-squared mixing gap, and singular-covariance-safe Gaussian mapping do not yield whole-array uniform inference without a uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization condition.
body.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 B_0=\frac{6373}{30000},\qquad x_0=\frac18,
 \qquad \bar b_0=\frac78,qquad t_0=\frac{5123}{10000},
 \qquad c_0=t_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Then
\[
 t_0+B_0+x_0=4B_0,qquad \eta_0=\frac14,qquad
 c_0^2B_0=\frac{B_0}{t_0}=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa.
\]
Set \(m_j=j\), so \(j/m_j=1\).

For each sufficiently large integer \(q\), define a whole array \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\).  Every row is independent and identically distributed over the two-sided time index.  In each row \(j\ne q\), generate mutually independent
\[
 F_t\sim N(0,B_0),\quad e_{1t},e_{2t}\sim N(0,x_0),
 \quad \varepsilon_{0t}\sim N(0,\bar b_0),
\]
and set
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\quad \Delta_t=\tau,
 \quad W_{1t}=c_0(F_t+e_{1t}),\quad W_{2t}=c_0(F_t+e_{2t}).
\]
In row \(j=q\), retain \(F_t\sim N(0,B_0)\), put \(p_q=q^{-2}\), \(a_q=q^{-4}\), generate mutually independent
\[
 I_{q,t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_q),qquad
 Z_{0t},Z_{1t},Z_{2t}\sim N(0,1),
\]
and use the same observation equations with
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}=I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},qquad
 e_{1t}=a_qZ_{1t},qquad e_{2t}=a_qZ_{2t}.
\]
The rare centered component is thus in the untreated-outcome error and treatment remains constant.  Conditional on \(F_t\), all three idiosyncratic errors are independent, and \(\mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\Delta_t=\tau\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M(0)\).  Independence over time proves stationarity and \(\beta_j(h)=0\) for \(h\geq1\).  Gaussian scales are bounded, \(0\leq I_{q,t}\leq1\), and \(a_q,p_q\leq1\), so one finite \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) bounds all required moments over \(j,q\).  For either role and every row,
\[
 M_s=c_0^2B_0=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa,qquad
 \mathbb E(Z_{s,t}Y_t(0))=c_0B_0=M_s/c_0.
\]
Therefore \(\alpha_s=c_0^{-1}\), and the bridge residual is \(\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t}\), where \(e_{s,t}\) is the selected donor's measurement error.  It is centered, and
\[
 \mathbb E\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s\}=\tau.
\]
The two controls have identical joint second moments with the treated outcome in every row, so their population ridge coefficients and losses coincide: \(L_{1,j}=L_{2,j}\).  Thus the bounded selector-gap condition holds with envelope zero.

Since \(\mathbb EW_{D_s,t}=0\), \(H_s=0\), \(\psi_{s,t}=0\), and \(A_s=0\).  All rows after \(q\) equal the ordinary Gaussian row, so their long-run covariance matrices are constant and converge to a finite positive-semidefinite matrix.  The stacked limit is singular because both pre-ATT coordinates vanish.  A possibly singular Gaussian limit nevertheless exists: for the ordinary-row centered score vector \(G_t\) and every fixed \(u\),
\[
 \mathbb E\exp(\mathrm iu^{\prime}G_t/\sqrt j)
 =1-\frac{u^{\prime}\Sigma_Gu}{2j}+O(j^{-3/2}),
\]
and independence followed by exponentiation proves convergence of every multivariate characteristic function to the possibly singular Gaussian characteristic function, without covariance inversion.

For an ordinary row the ridge fitted value is \(\eta_0(F_t+e_{jt})\).  With \(U_t=(1-\eta_0)F_t+\varepsilon_{0t}\), the loss contrast is
\[
 \ell_{1,t}-\ell_{2,t}
 =-2\eta_0U_t(e_{1t}-e_{2t})+eta_0^2(e_{1t}^2-e_{2t}^2).
\]
The summands are uncorrelated, \(\operatorname{Var}(e_1-e_2)=2x_0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(e_1^2-e_2^2)=4x_0^2\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)
 =4\eta_0^2\{(1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0\}(2x_0)
 +4\eta_0^4x_0^2.
\]
Since \((1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0=159119/160000\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{159119}{2560000}+\frac1{4096}
 =\frac{39}{625}>\nu.
\]
The post residual is \(v_{s,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t}\), whose ordinary-row variance is \(\bar b_0+x_0=1\).  With \(r=1\) and \(A_s=0\),
\[
 V_s=V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=1>\nu.
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathcal M(0)\) now hold.  The factor representation, constant effect, conditional error independence, nonzero square bridge, and rowwise domination established in \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\) also place these arrays in the stated common published subclass.

Analyze row \(q\).  Let \(\mathcal N_q\) be the event that \(I_{q,t}=0\) for every \(t\in\mathcal B_q\cup\mathcal C_q\).  It is independent of \(\mathcal F_A\), and, because the two future blocks contain at most \(2q\) observations,
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal N_q)\geq(1-q^{-2})^{2q}\to1.
\]
The early label is \(\mathcal F_A\)-measurable.  Fix either possible selected donor \(j\), with opposite proxy \(k\).  On \(\mathcal N_q\), the true bridge residual is
\[
 r_{j,t}^0=-p_q+a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt}).
\]
The exact future-only bridge definition gives, except on the null event \(\widehat M_{B,j}=0\),
\[
 \widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j
 =\widehat M_{B,j}^{-1}N_{B,q}^{-1}
  \sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal N_q\), Gaussian laws and Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
 \widehat M_{B,j}=c_0^2B_0+O_P(q^{-1/2}),quad
 \overline W_{k,B}=O_P(q^{-1/2}),quad
 \widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j
 =O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1/2}\},
\]
uniformly over \(j=1,2\).  Similarly \(\overline W_{j,C}=O_P(q^{-1/2})\).  Hence the exact post average satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{B,C,j}-\tau
 &=\overline r_{j,C}^0-(\widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j)\overline W_{j,C}\\
 &=-p_q+O_P(a_qq^{-1/2})+O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1}\}
 =-p_q\{1+o_P(1)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For any centered scalar observations \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), the Bartlett quadratic form obeys
\[
 0\leq\widehat\Omega_g\leq(2h+1)N^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ng_t^2,
\]
by \(2|g_tg_{t-j}|\leq g_t^2+g_{t-j}^2\).  The centered fitted post residual differs from \(a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt})\) by the centered version of \(-(\widehat\alpha_{B,j}-\alpha_j)W_{jt}\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{v,C,j}
 =O_P\left[h_q\left\{a_q^2+\frac{(p_q+a_q)^2}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
The precise future-only sensitivity is \(\widehat H_{B,C,j}=-\widehat\mu_{C,j}^{\prime}\widehat M_{B,j}^{-1}=O_P(q^{-1/2})\).  Before its multiplication, the fitted bridge score has conditional second moment \(O_P(p_q^2+a_q^2)\), so
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{\psi,B,j}=O_P\{h_q(p_q^2+a_q^2)/q\}.
\]
Since \(N_{B,q}\asymp q\), \(m_q=q\), \(h_q=O(q^{1/5})\), and \(a_q\leq p_q\),
\[
 \widehat S_{j,q}^2
 =O_P\left\{\frac{h_qa_q^2}{q}+\frac{h_qp_q^2}{q^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat S_{j,q}}{p_q}=o_P(1).
\]
Because \(a_q>0\), the centered post residual vector contains a nonconstant continuous Gaussian component almost surely.  The Bartlett quadratic form is nonnegative and its zero set is a proper algebraic subset of that continuous vector; hence \(\widehat S_{j,q}>0\) almost surely for large \(q\), so the nonpositive fallback is not invoked.  Combining numerator and denominator bounds yields, on \(\mathcal N_q\),
\[
 T_q=\frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
 {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}\to-\infty
\]
in probability, uniformly over both possible early labels.  Since \(\Pr(\mathcal N_q)\to1\), the same divergence holds unconditionally.

Choose deterministic \(b_q\to\infty\) so slowly that \(\Pr(T_q>-b_q)\to0\), and put
\[
 K_q=\sup_x\left|\Pr(T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A)-\Phi(x)\right|.
\]
Evaluation at \(-b_q\) and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb EK_q\geq
 \left|\Pr(T_q\leq-b_q)-\Phi(-b_q)\right|\to1.
\]
Since every Kolmogorov distance is at most one, \(\mathbb EK_q\to1\).  This is the asserted maximal failure.
body.justification: The diagonal counterexample identifies the exact whole-array quantifier failure and sharpens the conditional Gaussian-approximation error to its maximal possible value.
body.gap: Pointwise covariance limits and limiting variance margins do not control the finite row at which a supremum over whole arrays is evaluated.
body.consumer: Together with the stabilized-class theorem, this establishes a positive/negative design boundary based on common finite-row horizon comparability and scalar variance stabilization for the proposed correction.
